assumptions: `transfer` is the sole mutator of `bal` among the seven guarded operations — verified by reading resource.mjs at this revision, not by a checker (ASM-TRANSFER-SOLE-MUTATOR)
attrs.evidence: PROOF. `admissibleTransfer(L,res,from,to,amt)` is the sole guard on `transfer`, which is the sole balance-mutating primitive among transfer/spend/refill/allocate/charge/use/repair. It requires `amt >= 0`, and for `kind[res] === 'irreversible'` it returns false when `from === SINK`. An accepted transfer therefore changes only `bal[from][res] -= amt` and `bal[to][res] += amt` with `amt >= 0` and `from !== SINK`; so `bal[SINK][res]` is touched only in the `to === SINK` case, where it increases by `amt >= 0`. Non-decreasing follows, and a transfer with `from === SINK` returns INFEASIBLE by the same clause. This is the proposition LED-C9 was reaching for and did not state: LED-C9 quantified over EVERY operation of the module, and `consolidate`/`forget` are operations of the module that are not transfer-mediated.
attrs.review_focus: The proof leans on `transfer` being the sole mutator among the seven guarded operations. That was verified by reading all 167 lines of resource.mjs, not by a checker. If a later round adds an eighth operation that writes `bal` directly, this proof goes stale silently — which is the same failure mode as LED-C9 and is not yet mechanically refused.
attrs.statement: For a resource declared `irreversible`, every operation routed through `admissibleTransfer` leaves the sink balance non-decreasing, and any transfer out of SINK is INFEASIBLE.
